semantic_correction.stem: A parent asks whether an out-of-range newborn screening result means the baby definitely has the condition. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: It means the baby might have the condition, so timely follow-up testing is needed to determine whether the diagnosis is present.
options.B: It confirms the diagnosis, so additional testing is generally unnecessary before treatment decisions are made.
options.C: It can be ignored while the baby appears well because follow-up is needed after symptoms develop.
options.D: It indicates that screening was performed because the baby already had symptoms or a strong family history.

semantic_correction.rationale: HRSA explains that newborn screening and diagnostic testing are not the same. Screening identifies babies who might have a condition; it does not determine with certainty whether the condition is present. An out-of-range result means the baby needs additional testing, often diagnostic testing, and follow-up may need to occur right away because early diagnosis and treatment can be important even when the newborn appears well. Therefore option A is the most accurate response.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Explain that newborn screening identifies risk rather than confirming diagnosis and that out-of-range results require timely follow-up testing even when the infant appears well.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the uniquely long correct answer, and preserved HRSA's screening-versus-diagnosis distinction plus the need for timely follow-up after an out-of-range result.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately teaches that an out-of-range newborn screen is not a definitive diagnosis and requires prompt follow-up testing.

option_audit.A: Correct. HRSA states that out-of-range screening indicates possible disease and requires follow-up testing, often diagnostic testing.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Screening does not by itself establish a definitive diagnosis.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Follow-up should not wait for symptoms; some conditions require rapid confirmation and early treatment.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Newborn screening is routine population screening and is not limited to symptomatic or high-family-risk infants.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone correctly distinguishes screening from diagnosis and states the appropriate next step.
cueing_check: All four options are interpretations of an out-of-range result of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
